name: shooting-stars

frames.best_why: Long bright streak cuts diagonally across the middle with its fading tail.

tagline: Thin meteor streaks dart across a dark starry page now and then.
summary: A transparent overlay that launches a single glowing streak from a random screen edge every few seconds. Each one races diagonally across and fades off-frame.
appearance: A near-black field dusted with faint stars. Now and then a thin bright streak, white or tinted blue, cuts diagonally across the frame with a soft fading tail.
behaviour: On a randomised delay a new streak starts at a random screen edge and races across at a random speed, growing slightly as it goes before vanishing off-frame. Nothing responds to the pointer.
demo_content: Heading 'Shooting Star × Star Background' over a faint starfield; the demo mounts a separate star background too.
search_phrases: falling star streaks in the night sky
occasional bright line across a dark page
space backdrop with darting light trails
diagonal streak that crosses the screen
starry black page with rare flashes
comet effect behind a product launch
use_when: A dark hero needs a sparse sense of motion and depth without distracting from the copy.
avoid_when: Streaks appear at random, so the effect can look empty for long stretches, and it never stops.
customise: Tune minSpeed, maxSpeed, minDelay, maxDelay, star width and height, and the two gradient colours. Screen-edge starts and the growth rate are fixed.
weight_why: One SVG rect moved with requestAnimationFrame, plus a timer for the next star.

a11y.note: A purely decorative loop with no reduced-motion guard, and the streaks are invisible to assistive tech by design.

issues: The star dust in the frames comes from another component mounted by the demo.
Streaks are so rare that frames 3 and 4 show almost no motion at all.
polish_why: Clean tapered streaks over a star field; the effect is too sparse to notice most of the time.
title: Shooting Stars
